study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Tong et al., Journal of Affective Disorders, 2024
study_identification_part.si4_title: Individual deviations from normative electroencephalographic connectivity predict antidepressant response

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract clearly states the study’s objective: to develop a normative modeling framework from healthy EEG connectivity to quantify individual deviations and use these deviations to predict antidepressant treatment outcomes (sertraline and placebo). It also describes the purpose of applying normative modeling (personalized treatment and understanding psychopathological dimensions). Both criteria are satisfied.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "Here we develop a novel normative modeling framework to quantify individual deviations..."; "We built a normative model with resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) connectivity data from healthy controls... we trained sparse predictive models for treatment responses of MDD patients..."; "off ers a promising avenue for the personalized treatment"

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: This is a NEW normative model. Eligibility criteria for healthy controls are described for each cohort (EMBARC healthy, Depression-EEG, LEMON), including inclusion/exclusion. Data completeness is described at least for LEMON (excluding subjects without rsEEG). The final healthy sample used for the norm is stated as 154 young adults (8 EMBARC, 75 Depression-EEG, 71 LEMON). However, explicit image quality standards for the healthy reference cohorts (e.g., motion/artifact thresholds) are not fully specified in the main text; acquisition/QC is deferred to Supplementary methods, but detailed QC criteria are described generally for EEG preprocessing across cohorts rather than cohort-specific exclusion thresholds. Therefore, some but not all criteria are satisfied.

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age is explicitly handled: the normative model is built on 18–25-year-old healthy controls to calibrate demographics, and age is included as a covariate during ComBat harmonization across cohorts. Site effects are addressed via empirical Bayes harmonization (ComBat) using cohort as batch labels. Sex is not mentioned as a covariate in the normative modeling. Thus, covariates are handled partially (age and site), but not comprehensively (e.g., sex not specified).

The batch labels were assigned based on the cohort origin ... Notably, as cohorts had different age ranges, we incorporated age as a covariate in the data harmonization..."

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: No application of the normative model to an independent external healthy dataset (not used in model development) is described. The normative model was built by combining three cohorts of healthy controls, and while cross-validation is mentioned, there is no explicit external validation on a held-out healthy dataset not used in training.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: No explicit external validation of the healthy norm is reported.

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical approach is described in detail: an autoencoder trained in MATLAB (trainAutoencoder) with L2 constraint and sigmoid activations to reconstruct EEG FC for healthy controls; individual deviations are the reconstruction error. Baselines with PCA and regression-based reconstructions are also described. Software and libraries are named (MATLAB, Brainstorm).
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "we used the MATLAB function 'trainAutoencoder' ... L2-norm constraint ... sigmoid activation ... reconstructed EEG FC ... reconstruction error ... quantification of individual deviation"; "PCA-based ... regression-based ..."
